BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Bottom line

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. It accepts several of our fallback numbers without authority, shifts the known diligence issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, title) onto the Buyer, and asks us to treat the whole package as closed. We should not accept any of it on that basis.

## Process points first

- **"[STANDARD]", "FINAL", "market standard", "settled at principal level" and "pre-cleared" are assertions, not authority.** Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, none of these labels clears a position. Nothing in the file shows Amelia Frost approved any of this. The reviewer note asking us to skip [STANDARD] clauses is declined. Every clause is in scope.
- **The Seller's 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) and 18-month period match our conditional fallbacks, but neither is usable.** The 20% cap needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft, and the 18-month period needs her written approval. Neither has been given. A matching number does not make a position cleared.
- **We have only a summary, not the full SPA draft.** Clause numbers (e.g. 3/6.3, 2/7, 9.3/12.8/20.5) are cited inconsistently and cannot be verified. Our mark-up should be checked against the actual SPA text.
- **Do not disclose our internal fallbacks or authority status in the mark-up.**

## Departures from playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Our playbook | Push back |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m (20% fallback only with written authority; none given) | Reject. Restate 25% / AUD 6m. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, deductible (excess only) | AUD 50,000, tipping (first dollar once exceeded) | Reject. Restate tipping basket. |
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Amelia Frost approval; none given) | Reject. Restate 24 months. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims" | Caps, time limits and bars apply to all claims | Fundamental, Title, fraud separated | Reject. |
| Fundamental / Title | Same caps and time limits as general | Separate regime: 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance | Apply to all claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum extent enforceable; not waivable | Reject. Restore carve-out. |
| Disclosure | Whole data room, public registers, Accounts | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject all general and deemed disclosure. |
| Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3) | Blanket exclusion including data room and public records | Delete; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Delete. |
| Bluefen consent | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of consent | Effective consent and evidence conditions satisfied before Completion | Reject. Consent is a pre-Completion condition. |
| Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) | Release provided after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Reject. |
| Employee bonuses (AUD 420k) | Not itemised; "matter for the Seller" | Specific line item or seller-funded, including triggered on-costs; funds flow must not silently exclude | Reject. |
| Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure | Reject. |
| DD-006 export incident | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or demand | Reject the materiality characterisation; require the steps below. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt or price deduction | Reject the characterisation; assess first. |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. Keep as separate categories. |
| Title | DD-012 share register | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is internal, not independent | Reject. |

## Material issues and reasoning

### 1. Risk allocation: the package is worse than the headline numbers suggest

The combined effect of the cap, thresholds, time limits and reliance provisions is significant. Take a AUD 1m warranty breach:

- **Playbook:** The basket is exceeded, so the Seller pays from the first dollar: AUD 1m (within the AUD 6m cap).
- **Seller's package:** The Seller pays AUD 750k after the AUD 250k deductible.

That is a AUD 250k loss on one claim. Any single claim under AUD 25k is irrecoverable. Claims must be notified within 18 months. Title and fraud claims sit under the same limits, which is unacceptable. Fraud should not be subject to any cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy or non-reliance clause, to the maximum extent enforceable.

### 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge would swallow the diligence findings

The Disclosure Letter discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room (DL 1.1), including DD-002 to DD-012, and the public registers (DL 1.2). Combined with cl. 8.3, which bars claims for anything discoverable in the data room, this means every issue we have identified in diligence would be disclosed and unclaimable. The specific issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006) would then have no warranty remedy at all.

We need specific fair disclosure and special handling (specific indemnities or price mechanics) for each known issue. We should not rely on the general warranty regime for them.

### 3. Completion mechanics leave the Buyer carrying known liabilities

- **Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue):** The DL confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Treating consent as satisfied on delivery, under reasonable endeavours, would let Completion occur without the consent that protects a material customer relationship. The DL's general non-admission (DL 1.4) that no consent is "legally required" must not be used to undercut the Bluefen requirement.
- **Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m):** The facility is unpaid and security is not discharged. A post-Completion release leaves the Company, and therefore us, exposed to the facility and its security. Repayment must come from Completion funds, with effective releases in hand.
- **Bonuses (AUD 420k):** DL 5 confirms the amounts are absent from the funds flow, and it does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply. Either the amount and any triggered on-costs are a specific funds-flow line, or the Seller funds them. "A matter for the Seller" is not a funding mechanism. We need the on-costs quantified before settlement.

### 4. Ironquay IP

The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. DD-010 records AUD 180k open, but that is not bank verification and no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists (DL 4). We should not assume the AUD 180k is owed or not owed. The indemnity should be broadened to cover the IP and the SOW3 cure, and we should obtain bank confirmation and an Ironquay position.

### 5. DD-006 export and privacy incident

The Seller describes this as preliminary and "not expected to be material". The DL confirms the material does not establish unauthorised access, exact scope or notification requirements, and it states no loss amount. We should not characterise it as a breach, and we should not accept the Seller's view that it is immaterial. We should require:

- Preservation of logs and the download link history
- An investigation scope, timetable and regular updates
- Confirmation of whether any notification obligation (e.g. under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth)) is engaged, as a question for investigation counsel rather than an assumption
- Consideration of specific protection (indemnity or escrow) pending the outcome, subject to Amelia Frost's authority

Under the playbook, we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.

### 6. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)

The Seller calls the three renewals ordinary-course costs. DL 8 says the disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable or accrued. The three AUD 110k renewals should be read together, since they may form a single arrangement. We should assess them against the contracts and obtain the terms. There should be no automatic Debt classification or price deduction without that assessment.

### 7. Tax and IP

The Seller says these positions are "settled under the general regime". They are not. Under the playbook they remain OPEN, with no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution. They should be kept as separate categories with their own terms.

### 8. Title

The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register. That is an internal, supplied source, not independent proof of title (DL 10 confirms the Buyer has not verified title). We should require:

- Independent company and ASIC extracts
- Searches for security interests (including PPSR) and other encumbrances
- Evidence of the Seller's capacity and authority to sell
- Confirmation that the register is complete and up to date

### 9. Third-party consents: lease and Mossvale

DL 7 and DL 9 do not say whether landlord or Mossvale consent is required for the share sale. These should be verified against the lease and the Mossvale agreement, and the Seller should confirm its position in writing.

## Recommendations

**Mark-up priorities (reject and restate):**

1. Cap at 25% / AUD 6m; de minimis AUD 5k; tipping basket AUD 50k; 24-month general period.
2. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
3. Fraud carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
4. Specific fair disclosure only. Delete data-room, public-register and deemed disclosure.
5. Delete the cl. 8.3 blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion.
6. Bluefen consent and evidence of satisfied conditions as a pre-Completion condition.
7. Riverlark repaid from Completion funds with effective releases; no post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
8. Bonuses (AUD 420k) and triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line or Seller-funded.
9. Broaden the Ironquay indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure.
10. Tax and IP kept open and in separate categories.

**Information requests:**

- Bluefen consent and evidence of satisfied cl. 11.3 conditions
- Riverlark payout letter and draft releases
- Bonus calculations, on-cost estimates and funds flow
- Ironquay bank records and assignment position for the AUD 180k
- DD-006 logs, investigation scope and timetable
- Sandbar contracts and renewal terms
- Independent title and encumbrance searches
- Lease and Mossvale consent analysis

**Internal actions before responding:**

- Confirm with Amelia Frost which positions, if any, she has authorised. Do not treat the Seller's figures as agreed.
- Obtain the full SPA draft to verify clause references.
- Decide whether DD-006 warrants a specific protection, and seek Amelia Frost's authority.
